The first paragraph makes sense, this doesn't as much.  Why wouldn't we just load the appropriate files in the unit test and bypass the filesystem altogether?

For integration tests we want to cover a large amount of code.

For proper testing, we need both the unit test (single component)
and integration test (everything working together).

Integration tests are very useful to prevent regressions and it's beneficial to run them close to the code path which would be run on a real system.

IMO it would make sense to make this change anyways, independent of any tests, but it's required for integration testing so i am doing it as part of this series.
partial review.

We already have a configuration class here, we should probably do at least some naming conventions to make sure that "Configuration" and "SystemConfiguration" aren't mistaken for one another, and the classes are clear.

Alternatively, I suspect these should just be the same object?

> Alternatively, I suspect these should just be the same object?

The main difference between `Configuration` class and `SystemConfiguration` class
is that `Configuration` class represents the configuration as it was loaded and 

`SystemConfiguration` represents whatever caching EM wants to persist for later use.

### separate purpose

So in terms of SRP principle ❤️ `Configuration` has responsibility to load the configuration (which does not change) and `SystemConfiguration` is for persistence of files representing current system state which does change.

### separate filesystems

`class Configuration` works on  `/usr/share/`
https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/FHS_3.0/fhs/ch04s11.html

and `class SystemConfiguration` works on `/var/`
https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/FHS_3.0/fhs/ch05.html

which can be neatly separated.

The 2 classes do not need to share information, they have no overlap, and they do not have pointers to each other. I'm 95% sure they cannot even reach each over via any of their member functions.

So i would prefer to keep them separate.

> we should probably do at least some naming conventions to make sure that "Configuration" and "SystemConfiguration" aren't mistaken for one another, and the classes are clear.

100% agree. I renamed to it to `class ConfigCache` to clarify the purpose and align with the variable name used for the instance throughout the patch.

Let me know if you find a better name 👍
I'm a little confused here, why does the DBUS interface need to know about filesystem directories?  that seems like a strange encapsulation of concerns?
configuration changes are persisted to file when `AddObject` API is used which is part of EMDBusInterface class. That's why it needs a pointer to `SystemConfiguration`
Just pass this by const reference if you're going to immediately make a ref-copy.

Was this comment here when you started the refactor?  Think it still holds and this can't just be info?

It's an old comment which was there before.

If it will be stored and persisted in journal depends on journal policy so if someone made it error before maybe for them `info` level is not stored / persisted?

Anyways, logging it as an error is misrepresenting it since it's not an error.
And it's not in line with other similar logs.

Adjusted it to be `info` level, thanks for pointing it out 👍
